items.title: Aging Parents and Empty Nests Force Homeowners To Rethink Layouts Years Before the Move
items.summary:
Most homeowners know their homes may need updates to accommodate their changing needs as they age.

Some, however, are thinking even further ahead.

Instead of waiting until those changes are necessary, they’re investing in renovations years in advance to prepare for aging parents who might eventually move in after their children leave the nest.

Angi’s 2026 State of Home Spending Pulse study found that 66% of homeowners plan to make a major home investment within the next five years. And the 2027 Home Trends To Watch report predicts that 2027 will be the year they take a proactive approach and focus on creating a home that grows with them.

If you own your home, experts agree that you should anticipate how your needs could change in the next five to 10 years and use that information to guide your long-term home improvement goals today.

By doing so, you can make the most out of your renovation budget, avoid costly last-minute adjustments, and ensure your home comfortably adapts to the different stages of life.

What's driving this trend? 

Matt Plaskoff, CEO and founder of One Week Bath in Los Angeles , is seeing this proactive, multigenerational "future-proofing” trend among his clients. 

“It comes down to people having heard stories of it going the other way. Mom falls or receives a diagnosis, and suddenly the family is trying to put in a walk-in shower and grab bars on short notice while suddenly incurring more costs with doctors and insurance,” says Plaskoff.

Multigenerational living is also at an all-time high, and the recent National Association of Realtors®…
items.t: Aging Parents and Empty Nests Force Homeowners To Rethink Layouts Years Before the Move

items.title: Inside the Properties James Bond Has Made Famous as Robert Pattinson Gears Up to Play 007
items.summary:
It’s official: Robert Pattinson is stepping into the role of James Bond .

The news comes after years of speculation surrounding who might succeed Daniel Craig —who was the sixth actor to bring 007 to life, and portrayed the British spy in five films, ending with 2021’s “No Time To Die.”

The official James Bond X account shared a first look of Pattinson donning the infamous tux for the role, captioned “Identity Confirmed.”

“James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honor of a lifetime,” Pattinson said in a statement . “To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement.”

Director Denis Villeneuve alluded to the search for the next Bond in the statement.

Robert Pattinson has been announced as the next James Bond. He's the seventh actor to bring Agent 007 to life. (Photo by Dia Dipasupil/Getty Images) 

“I want to express my deep gratitude to the remarkable actors who joined us on this journey,” the “Dune” director said. “We were surrounded by extraordinary talent, but there can only be one 007.”

Dozens of potential candidates have been floated as possibilities since Craig’s reign came to an end, including Idris Elba , Jacob Elordi , Callum Turner , and John Hardy .

Bond first walked onto the silver screen in 1962, when Sean Connery brought the iconic book character to life in the first film, “Dr. No.” There have been a whopping 25 Bond films so far, with Pattinson suiting up for the 26th.

After seven films, Connery ended his run in 1983 with “Never Say Never.” In 1969, George Lazenby became the only…
items.t: Inside the Properties James Bond Has Made Famous as Robert Pattinson Gears Up to Play 007

items.title: Jennifer Lopez Celebrates ‘Freedom’ as an Empty Nester Since Her Twins Left California Home for College
items.summary:
Jennifer Lopez has admitted that she is enjoying the "freedom" that comes with living alone after her 18-year-old twins, Max and Emme , left their California home for college.

The 57-year-old singer and actress —who is attempting to sell her and ex-husband Ben Affleck 's $50 million marital mansion —once again opened up about the realities of being an empty nester while appearing on "The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon." 

The singer , who shares the twins with ex-husband Marc Anthony , admitted that she "cried for six months straight" when her twins headed off to college.

Although Lopez confessed it has been "emotional," she insisted it has also been an "amazing" journey.

“It’s all the feelings. It’s like one of those moments in life where you’re just, you’re sad, you’re melancholy, but you’re excited and you’re hopeful—there’s just so many feelings that go with [it]. I cried for, like, six months straight, like, two months before they graduated until I dropped them off and then a few weeks after that," she said.

Jennifer Lopez has admitted she is enjoying the "freedom" that comes with living alone after her 18-year-old twins, Max and Emme, left their California home for college. (Instagram/Jennifer Lopez)

The A-lister admitted that she is now getting comfortable with the "freedom" she has living alone.

“It’s the first [time] since I was, I don’t know, in my early 20s that I haven’t been with someone, had my kids. I’m alone, I’m…

items.title: Nantucket Brokerage Must Pay $1.3 Million to Buyers Who Couldn’t Expand Their Home as Desired
items.summary:
A Massachusetts judge and jury have ordered a Nantucket real estate firm to pay nearly $1.3 million to a couple after finding that one of its agents misrepresented whether a home could be expanded to fit their family of eight.

The yearslong legal battle centered on a twp-bedroom, 1,200 square-foot property purchased by Dr. Mary Murray and Jeff Ment. Murray, an obstetrician, and Ment, a lawyer, live in Westport, CT , but spend summers with their six children in Nantucket, MA.

Their kids “all love to be there. Every single one of them loves to be on the island, and we love to be with them,” Murray tells Realtor.com® . 

Their real estate agent, Melanie Gowen , helped them find rentals in previous years, and in 2020, she represented them in their purchase of 151 P olpis Road for $1.41 million. 

Murray says the home wasn’t ideal, but in the ultracompetitive Nantucket market, where the median listing price is $5,995,000, they felt lucky to buy anything at all. 

And Murray says the family was reassured after Gowen, an agent with William Raveis Nantucket, told the couple they’d have no problem building an addition to accommodate their six children. 

“She said, ‘Listen, I know it’s the smallest house, but it’s a great buy. The best part about this is it’s an undersized house on an oversized piece of property that you can double,’” Murray says. 

According to the couple, Gowen said she went to the island’s building department and confirmed expansion was possible. She’d even sketched out the addition and sent a video of the planned build, Murray says. 

In Nantucket, rules…
items.t: Nantucket Brokerage Must Pay $1.3M to Buyers Who Couldn’t Expand Their Home as Desired

items.title: Landlord With Dark Past Is Charged With the Murder of Disabled Tenant Who Was ‘Late on Rent’
items.summary:
A New Mexico landlord accused of murdering his disabled tenant and burying the body beneath the porch of the victim’s home gave conflicting accounts about whether he had evicted the man over purported unpaid rent, according to court documents.

Jonah Jeter , 33, was charged last week in Albuquerque with murder, aggravated burglary, and three counts of tampering with evidence in the death of Robert Debeary , 51, whose remains were discovered in October, more than two months after his family reported him missing.

For nearly five years, Debeary, a four-time stroke survivor, lived in an apartment at 233 Alcazar St. NE, where he received housing assistance through the federal Section 8 program, according to the criminal complaint filed in Bernalillo County Metropolitan Court.

Debeary, who walked with a cane after becoming paralyzed on one side of his body, regularly kept in touch with his loved ones, so when a week passed without hearing from him, his family grew concerned, according to his future daughter-in-law, Latajanae Evangelista , who spoke with Realtor.com® . 

In mid-August, Debeary’s brother contacted Albuquerque Community Safety to request a welfare check, but was told that he had been evicted from the apartment the previous week. His family questioned that account, saying he had never mentioned facing eviction despite complaining of “ongoing issues” with Jeter.

“He was just a man, a disabled man living in his home, and he would never just go missing. He would never leave his family,” Evangelista tells Realtor.com in a phone interview, her voice breaking as she…
items.t: Landlord With Dark Past Is Charged With the Murder of Disabled Tenant Who Was ‘Late on Rent’

items.title: Drake Maye Suffers Potentially Season-Ending Ankle Injury—Inside His Massachusetts Home Where He Could Recover
items.summary:
New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye could miss the rest of the 2026 season after injuring his ankle against the Detroit Lions in Munich.

According to reports, the athlete may have fractured his ankle. Maye was hurt on the Patriots’ first possession of the Week 10 matchup when Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson sacked him on third-and-goal. 

The third-year quarterback was evaluated on the sideline before walking to the locker room. New England later ruled him out with an ankle injury. Tommy DeVito is the Patriots' backup quarterback. 

Patriots coach Mike Vrabel offered few details after the game. On Monday morning, he told WEEI’s “The Greg Hill Show” that Maye had stayed in Germany as a precaution and was expected to return to the U.S. soon.

New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye could miss the rest of the 2026 season after injuring his ankle against the Detroit Lions in Munich. (Matthew J. Lee/The Boston Globe via Getty Images) 

“The update that I have is just out of caution, Drake stayed back,” Vrabel said, as quoted by the Boston Herald’s Doug Kyed . “He’ll be traveling back here shortly. But just wanted to make sure that everything was good for him to travel back and safely. The things that go around injuries, and just wanted to make sure everything was in line for him to travel, and it seems like he is. He’ll be returning here, I think, shortly.”

If Maye does end the season here, he will recover at his sprawling property, which his wife, Ann Michael , previously revealed a candid glimpse of.

Drake and Ann Michael, both 23, tied the knot in June…

items.title: Unlicensed Plumber Accused of Squatting and Subleasing Rooms in Senior Woman’s Home
items.summary:
A California woman who hired a plumber to make repairs to her home while she was living elsewhere says he took over the property, moved strangers into the house, and locked her out—sparking a two-year nightmare that left her fighting to reclaim her own home .

Jordy Smith , 76, said the man working on the plumbing at her home in San Diego's City Heights neighborhood allegedly transferred the utilities into his own name and began renting out rooms to strangers, pocketing the payments.

Smith and her partner, who owned the home, later discovered the man was not a licensed plumber; but by then, the situation had spiraled out of control. When the couple returned home, they were locked out of their own house and couldn’t get the new occupants to leave, she claimed. 

"He just took over and, like, before we knew it, there was like 15 people," Smith told ABC 10News . "Once that happened, it really made it look like to the homeless people that were coming in, that made it look like it was his house.”

The couple tried to confront the people living in the home but Smith said they had locked the door and wouldn’t talk. 

"I couldn't sleep at night," Smith said. "I mean, it just seemed like we'd never get back home."

Meanwhile, the property had attracted multiple visits by the police. San Diego police were called to the home more than 30 times between Jan. 1, 2024, and Aug. 17, 2026, for reports of suspected drug activity, trespassing, and smoke coming from the property, according to dispatch records. 

In an attempt to get the squatters removed from the property, Smith turned to…
items.t: Unlicensed Plumber Accused of Squatting and Subleasing Rooms in Senior Woman’s Home

The singer , 57, and the actress, 53, owned the residence for more than a decade , having purchased it for $1.1 million in 2015.

Described as "an extraordinary St. Charles estate," the property underwent extensive renovations during Wahlberg and McCarthy's time there, with the couple transforming it into a personalized retreat designed for both entertaining and relaxing.

Inside, the home boasts an expansive living room and family room, a formal dining room, den, game room, recreation space, exercise room, and finished lower level.

The kitchen comes with an island, breakfast bar, walk-in pantry, and butler's pantry, while hardwood and stone flooring can be found throughout much of the main level.

items.title: Inside Warren Buffett’s Surprisingly Modest Property Portfolio as He Steps Down as Berkshire Hathaway Chairman
items.summary:
Billionaire investor Warren Buffett has officially stepped down as chairman of Berkshire Hathaway—marking the end of an extraordinary era for the 96-year-old businessman, whose approach to real estate has long been almost as unconventional as his investing career.

Berkshire Hathaway announced on Sept. 18 that Buffett has been named chairman emeritus, effective immediately, while his son, Howard G. Buffett , has been elected chairman of the board. Buffett will remain a director and continue to offer his insight to the company. 

“As Chairman Emeritus, Mr. Buffett will remain a member of the Board of Directors and will continue to offer his valued judgment and perspective,” Berkshire said.

The transition comes months after Buffett relinquished his CEO duties to longtime Berkshire executive Greg Abel , completing a carefully planned changing of the guard at the company Buffett has been associated with since 1965. Berkshire Hathaway sold $426 million more in stocks than it bought in the third quarter of 2026 under Abel. It was the 15th quarter out of the past 16 in which the company’s stock sales exceeded its purchases.

"I have served Berkshire since 1965," Buffett said in a letter to shareholders, released alongside the announcement. "Sixty-plus years in, I still have the best job in the world."

items.title: HOA Trade Group Presses for More Protections After DC Shooter Targeted Building Manager
items.summary:
The trade group representing homeowners associations is calling for stronger protections after a shooting in Washington, DC , left a community manager dead.

The Community Association Institute said that it would renew efforts support laws that address harassment, threats, and intimidation against community managers before they escalate into violence. 

The group had pressed for such legislation in Nevada in 2025 and plans to do so at the federal level in 2027. New Jersey and Minnesota are also reportedly considering some legislation to address harassment.

Thursday's shooting in DC's Logan Circle neighborhood claimed the life of James “Jimmy” Stuart , manager of the Metropole and injured five others. The suspected shooter, Dr. Matt Wade Lambert , a resident of the complex, reportedly was in a dispute with the community over renovations he said damaged his penthouse unit.

“We mourn Jimmy's loss and extend our deepest condolences to his family, friends, colleagues, and the entire Metropole community,” the CAI statement reads. “Our thoughts are also with the other victims, residents, and building staff whose lives have been forever changed by this tragedy.”

Lambert was in the middle of a protracted legal dispute with his building's HOA at the time that the shooting happened. 

Social median posts reputedly made by him criticized the community for months after he alleged repairs caused water damage and mold. Police say that, after Lambert killed Stuart and injured four others, he subsequently took his own life during a police standoff.

Now, it has been revealed that she will be back in court in March 2027 to face a retrial on the same charges. 

The trial began on July 31, when the jurors traveled to Clancy's former home in Duxbury, MA , where her three children were found in the basement by their father, Patrick Clancy , on Jan. 24, 2023, having been strangled with exercise bands. 

According to the Associated Press , the jury was escorted into the home in groups of six and spent a total of 40 minutes at the property, walking through the entire abode, as well as the yard where Clancy was found after throwing herself out of her bedroom window in an apparent suicide attempt. 

Lindsay Clancy is set to face a second murder trial in March 2027. (David L. Ryan/The…

items.title: Lindsay Clancy’s Murder Retrial Set for March 2027—Inside the Massachusetts Home Where Her 3 Children Died
items.summary:
Lindsay Clancy is set to face a second murder trial on March 29, 2027—less than one year after her first case ended in a hung jury and more than three years after she was accused of murdering her three children inside the family's Massachusetts home.

Clancy, 36, has admitted to taking the lives of her daughter, Cora , 5, and sons Dawson , 3, and 8-month-old Callan , but has pleaded not guilty to the three first-degree murder charges against her, with her attorneys arguing that she was suffering from severe postpartum psychosis at the time of their deaths.

Over the course of the five-week trial, her defense team sought to convince jurors that Clancy should not be held legally accountable for the killings because of a "lack of criminal responsibility," according to the Boston Globe .

Following 19 hours of deliberation, the 12-person jury was declared deadlocked after telling state Judge William Sullivan it was unable to reach a unanimous verdict. Sullivan instructed the jurors to return to the deliberation room and continue their efforts to reach a verdict, before eventually declaring a mistrial. 

Then, mere weeks ago, Clancy returned to court, where her legal team attempted to argue that she can't be retried due to double jeopardy in hopes to have the charges dropped. Meanwhile, the prosecution asked the judge to decline the motion to dismiss the charges, claiming they could have a retrial.

Now, it has been revealed that the prosecution will be retrying Clancy on the same charges, with pretrial hearings scheduled for Dec. 30 and Feb. 18.

Lindsay Clancy is set to face…
items.t: Lindsay Clancy’s Murder Retrial Set for March 2027—Inside the Massachusetts Home Where Her Three Children Died

items.title: Robert Pattinson Named the Next James Bond—Months After Joking His Beverly Hills Move Made Him ‘Bougie’
items.summary:
Robert Pattinson is taking over as James Bond —months after the British actor revealed that he and Suki Waterhouse had traded Los Angeles ’ east side for a rental in Beverly Hills . 

The 40-year-old will succeed Daniel Craig in the 26th Bond film, becoming the seventh actor to play 007 in the official series.

Denis Villeneuve will direct the still-untitled movie, with Steven Knight writing the screenplay and Amy Pascal and David Heyman producing. Craig last appeared as the British spy in 2021’s "No Time to Die."

Five months before the casting announcement, Pattinson told GQ that he, Waterhouse, and their young daughter were renting a house in Beverly Hills. 

Robert Pattinson is taking over as James Bond—months after the British actor revealed that he and Suki Waterhouse had traded Los Angeles’ east side for a rental in Beverly Hills. (Laurent KOFFEL/Gamma-Rapho via Getty Images) 

The move took him to a part of town where he said he’d never lived. In his earlier years in Los Angeles, he owned a large home in Los Feliz, which he eventually sold. 

“I always thought I was an Eastside hipster guy. I would only ever come to Beverly Hills for my agency and stuff. Now I'm like, everything's kind of nice. Maybe I've turned bougie," he told the outlet. 

One feature of the rental had a practical purpose: its home gym. Pattinson told GQ he was using it to train for "The Batman: Part II," the sequel to his 2022 debut as the superhero. 

He recalled working out twice a day during preparations for his first turn as Batman and said that comments he’d made in interviews had given…
items.t: Robert Pattinson Named the Next James Bond—Months After Joking His Beverly Hills Move Made Him ‘Bougie’

items.title: Presley Gerber’s Hollywood Hills Home Hits the Market for $3.6 Million—Nearly 2 Months After His Death
items.summary:
Presley Gerber ’s Hollywood Hills home has hit the market for $3.59 million, less than two months after the model’s death at age 27.

The son of Cindy Crawford and Rande Gerber , who passed away on Sept. 20, snapped up the property for $3.4 million in March 2023. 

Now, nearly two months after his tragic death, the property has hit the market for $3.6 million with real estate agent Cindy Ambuehl of Christie's AKG , as first reported by TMZ .

The dwelling is described as "beautifully reimagined mid-century architecture meets modern luxury in the heart of the Hollywood Hills."

Inside, the main gathering space combines wood floors and a fireplace with access to the kitchen and dining areas.

items.title: Contractor at Site of Brooklyn Building Collapse Was Previously Sued for Negligence
items.summary:
The general contractor overseeing the construction site adjacent to a deadly building collapse in Brooklyn, NY, was previously accused in a lawsuit of compromising the structural integrity of nearby properties during an excavation project, court records show.

Signage at the construction site at 2625 Bedford Ave., as well as planning documents filed with the Department of Buildings, show that Townhouse Builders, Inc, doing business as Promont, was the general contractor overseeing the construction project.

Building records show that the project involved excavation work directly adjacent to the three-story mixed-use building at 1321 Flatbush Ave. that fully collapsed on Wednesday, killing eight people, including two children, and leaving 18 others injured.

The construction project had a documented history of safety concerns flagged by DOB inspectors, and Mayor Zohran Mamdani says there will be a full investigation into whether any issues at the Bedford Ave. construction site contributed to the collapse.

"If there is anyone or any entity operating in this city that bears responsibility for what happened, we will hold them accountable," the mayor said.

Now, court records reviewed by Realtor.com® show that Townhouse Builders was accused in a 2020 lawsuit of causing "a breached wall, substantial shifting, settlement and cracking" to an adjacent property during a separate construction job.

New York state records list Mordachai Waisbrod as the CEO of Townhouse Builders. The company and an attorney listed as representing the Townhouse in the 2020 lawsuit did not respond to…
items.t: Contractor at Site of Brooklyn Building Collapse Was Previously Sued for Negligence

items.title: Mapped: Where the Most Homeowners Own Their Homes Outright With No Mortgage
items.summary:
Roughly 3 in 5 American homeowners pay a mortgage every month, yet the share of those who own their property outright is steadily growing—with at least half of all homeowners in three states now completely mortgage-free .

According to a new Realtor.com® data analysis of the recently released 2025 American Community Survey 1-Year Estimates , 59% of homeowners carried a mortgage last year, while 41% owned their homes free and clear.

That marks a major shift from 2010, when fewer than a third of homes (32.8%) were owned outright while 67% carried home loan debt.

Mortgaged homeownership has shrunk across all four regions, though reliance on financing still varies significantly by geography. The West had the highest mortgage debt rate at 63.8%, while the South recorded the lowest at 56.8%. The Northeast and Midwest tied at 58.7%.

At the state level, West Virginia led the nation with 56.6% of its homeowners living mortgage-free, followed by Mississippi (52.7%) and New Mexico (50%).

On the other side of the spectrum, Washington, DC , in 2025 logged the lowest share of outright homeownership, at just 26.5%, trailed by Maryland (30.6%) and Colorado (31.6%).

Realtor.com senior economist Jiayi Xu explains that the balance between mortgaged and free-and-clear homes meaningfully shapes housing market dynamics, especially at a time when mortgage rates are high.

"Areas where owners rely more heavily on mortgages are more sensitive to rate changes, because monthly payments and the cost of moving both rise with borrowing costs," says Xu. "Areas with a higher share of outright…
items.t: Mapped: Where the Most Homeowners Own Their Homes Outright With No Mortgage

items.title: America’s Trillion-Dollar Credit Card Debt Threatens To Lock Millions Out of the Housing Market
items.summary:
With prices still alarmingly high, it comes as no surprise that Americans are increasingly turning to credit cards more than ever. 

But doing so could be silently sabotaging any hope of owning a home , if you’re not careful. 

Last week, the Federal Reserve Bank of New York published its latest household debt report .

Collectively, credit card balances climbed by $22 billion in the third quarter to a record $1.29 trillion. Balances are up 4.2% from a year earlier, and total household debt, including mortgages, auto loans, and student loans, expanded by $334 billion for the period to a record $19.1 trillion.

High levels of debt are problematic for anyone, but most especially for first-time homebuyers. If your ambitions for 2027 include buying a home, it’s important to get your debt in check before it’s too late.

Easy money comes at a price 

According to TransUnion’s most recent quarterly credit industry insights report , the number of people with credit cards rose 2% to 178 million up from 174.8 million.

The ease of use means most people turn to credit cards for their everyday purchases, like groceries, gas, and utility bills—all of which have seen a steep increase in prices over the past two years. 

Now, if you’re someone who pays off their credit card in full each month, you’re in the clear. If not, the average interest rate on a new credit card offer currently stands at about 24%, and debt can accumulate quickly. 

And this can cause an array of issues for first-time homebuyers. 

"Issues arising from high levels of consumer debt are amplified for first-time…
items.t: America’s Trillion-Dollar Credit Card Debt Threatens To Lock Millions Out of the Housing Market

items.title: How Training Veterans in Skilled Trades Could Speed Up Homebuilding and Ease Housing Costs
items.summary:
A severe shortage of skilled workers entering the residential construction sector has had a major impact on affordability, but the Home Builders Institute (HBI) believes the country’s large veteran population may be part of the solution.

The skilled labor shortage has led to an increase in construction time, with each home taking nearly two months longer to build, according to an HBI study . Due to the delays, there was a reduction of 19,000 homes built in 2024, representing an economic loss of over $8 billion, the study found.

Associated Builders and Contractors (ABC) estimated that the construction industry needs to attract roughly 349,000 net new workers in 2026 and 456,000 new workers in 2027 to meet demand for construction services.

There are a number of factors in the past 30 years that have led to the labor shortage, according to HBI CEO Ed Brady . First, a strong push for four-year degrees led many young people toward academic careers rather than trades. With more people retiring from the workforce than entering, the shortage began.

The issue was compounded during the financial crisis of 2008, when the residential construction field lost tons of skilled workers because there wasn’t enough work. Without enough housing construction, workers left for jobs in manufacturing and hospitality or retired early, according to Brady.

More recently, rocky immigration policies have challenged the skilled labor workforce, Brady explains.

When finding a solution to the shortage became dire, HBI believed that the veteran and transitioning military population was “an untapped…
items.t: How Training Veterans in Skilled Trades Could Speed Up Homebuilding and Ease Housing Costs

Listed for $2,888,000, the newly completed home was designed by Oshatz, an apprentice of Frank Lloyd Wright Jr. It is one of five planned homes tucked into the forest, four of which have yet to be built.

“It took about three years, but it is finally complete,” said listing agent Terry Sprague of LUXE | Forbes Global Properties . “Robert Oshatz is like the Andy Warhol/Peter Max of real estate. His designs are so completely unusual compared to commoditized architecture.”

items.title: Iconic 1960 Midcentury Modern ‘Wave House’ Is Back on the Market—With a Twist
items.summary:
Modernist architect Jules Gregory ’s iconic " Wave House ," which was offered together with a sleek studio in Lambertville, NJ, earlier this year is now available for individual purchase.

“The condo status was recently approved, so now you can get the Wave House for $1.65 million, the studio for $995,000, or both for $2.6 million,” says listing agent Grant Wagne r of Callaway Henderson Sotheby’s International Realty . “What makes this unique is if you wanted to buy both, you have the option to sell one later.”

Built in 1960, the four-bedroom primary residence, known for its wavy roofline, has 1,700 square feet of midcentury space, including curvy wood ceilings that rise and dip above the rooms, glass walls and doors, exposed beams, stone details, and oversized windows framing the picturesque lot.

Jules Gregory's "Wave House" in Lambertville, NJ, is now available for individual purchase. (Wiebke Martens) 

The living area features floor-to-ceiling windows to show off its dramatic roofline. (Wiebke Martens) 

The home features a European-inspired kitchen. (Wiebke Martens) 

“The Wave House will attract an architecture enthusiast drawn to its dramatic roofline, spaces that expand and compress, expanses of glass, and privacy,” Wagner says. “Being such a rare offering, it could easily bring a buyer from New York, Philadelphia, or abroad—someone who wants to own a piece of art in an architectural sense.”

With ceilings that appear to float above the living areas, the open floor plan also has a sunken conversation lounge, a beamed living room, and a European-inspired kitchen.…
items.t: Iconic 1960 Midcentury Modern ‘Wave House’ Is Back on the Market—With a Twist

items.title: Interest rate rises likely in coming months, Bank of England’s chief economist says
items.summary:
‘We have further to go,’ says Huw Pill after increase to 4% this month as Bank seeks to tackle rising inflation

The Bank of England will probably need to raise interest rates next month and again in early 2027 to combat rising inflation, its chief economist has said.

Signalling a sharp rise in mortgage payments for an estimated 2.3 million homeowners who will have to refinance their loans next year, Huw Pill said that while the decision to nudge interest rates from 3.75% to 4% earlier this month was a “significant step” towards getting monetary policy into a better place, “we ⁠have further to go”.

Aviva said on Friday it had experienced the jump amid an industry-wide surge in households filing subsidence claims with their insurers to cover repairs, which typically are needed to address cracks, sloping floors, and off-kilter doors and windows.
